correctness.rationale: Slater and stationarity yield clip(v/s) with s≥1; the unconstrained box projection suffices if it is ball feasible. Otherwise the squared norm of clip(v/s) drops strictly wherever it reaches the target with a nonzero free coordinate; a plateau at the target would require that all free inputs vanish and that the original box projection already be ball feasible. For a strict active pattern with k saturated outputs, the free output is √(r²−k)v_J/||v_J||₂ and its Jacobian is s⁻¹(I−uuᵀ). Apart from clipping coordinate planes, the switch on each clipping region lies in a level set of its clipped squared norm; at an active tie the saturated i satisfies (r²−k)v_i²=∑_{j in J}v_j². These are null sets for r²<n, with the r²=k degeneracy forcing all free inputs to vanish. With a=|u_i|, the maximum row sum is 1−a²+a∑_{j≠i}|u_j|; its Cauchy–Schwarz bound is attained by equal tail magnitudes whenever a lies in the stated interval. The interval is feasible since c_k>1/√m, and the change 2a²−1 gives the single clamped maximizer. One free coordinate contributes zero derivative. Euclidean nonexpansiveness ensures Lipschitz regularity; mollification with the a.e. derivative bound gives the global ℓ∞ bound. Conversely choose a strictly feasible equal-tail vector, scale the free input by s>1 and make the saturated inputs strictly larger than s. Test along the signs of the chosen row, then take s↓1 and approach any capped maximizer from inside; the identity regime separately gives one. At r=√5 in n=13 only k=0 and k=1 can beat the unrestricted bound for m≤11; both are upper-capped and F₁>F₀ reduces to 7>4√3. An independent arithmetic check gives excess 0.000500015579. For r≤1 only ordinary ball clipping is needed; at r↑√n the feasible intervals collapse to the equal-magnitude vectors and the largest limit is 2−2/n, while at redundancy coordinate clipping gives one.

value.rationale: Individual-coordinate error budgets and a joint energy cap naturally coexist. The exact global perturbation factor for the associated Euclidean projector, not merely an evaluation algorithm, quantifies their interaction. The tiny thirteen-dimensional gap is useful as a counterexample to the no-saturation simplification, not for its size, and the actual jump at redundancy separates stability of the sharp modulus from continuity of the sets.
